premises: Residual interstitial impurities (O, N) or minor compositional fluctuations are present in the initial single-phase HEA.
Under high stress and elevated temperature, these impurities become mobile and undergo stress-assisted diffusion.
This diffusion leads to localized solute segregation at grain boundaries and dislocations.
The segregation nucleates brittle intermetallic precipitates or second phases.
These brittle phases cause a loss of toughness and a transition to brittle fracture.
